# CLAUDE.md — DBMS EL Platform (CD252IA, RVCE)

Source of truth: `PROJECT_MASTER.md` (vision, schema, seed, verified queries, rubric). Approved plan: `docs/PLAN.md`.

## Hard rules
- PostgreSQL syntax only (Supabase, PG17). Vectors stay in pgvector; no separate vector DB; no LangChain. Retrieval is explicit SQL.
- MongoDB stays a real component (raw events, notes + immutable versions, portfolios).
- `supabase/fixture/` (01_schema, 02_seed, 03_queries) and `mongo/04_mongo.js` are the **frozen graded Test fixture**. Never edit them; Q1–Q37 / M1–M25 outputs must keep matching Appendix H. New schema changes go in migrations as append-only columns/constraints; new real data (P06, T00, [redacted]) goes in a separate demo seed.
- Faculty views expose metadata only. Enforce with RLS + `security_invoker` views; the AI layer queries as the requesting user, never with service_role.
- Never touch the Supabase project "Teron" or any project other than this one. Never delete the paused Tokyo project.
- Secrets: never commit `*.env`; never print secret values. Never read values from `atlas-credentials.env` into chat.
- No Teron/Metacognisync code or branding.

## Local
- Local PG17: `docker start elp-pg17` (port 54329, password `localdev`). Race check: `experiments/race/rr_trigger_check.sh`.
- Python via `uv` (3.12), Node 24. Tools via npx: `npx supabase`, `npx mongosh`, `npx vercel`.

# Plan — DBMS EL Platform (CD252IA): sharpened idea, upgrades, build plan, access checklist ## Context `PROJECT_MASTER.md` is the source of truth (vision, 13-table schema, seed, 37 SQL + 25 Mongo verified queries, rubric, open items). Synopsis + Component 4 (Test) are done; **no application code exists**. Arun asked for: a full plan using the whole master file, an improved idea, the biggest problems (idea + design), the best upgrades, and an exact list of what to hand over (esp. MongoDB) so Claude can run the project end-to-end. This plan merges 6 independent critiques (idea, grading, schema, architecture, privacy, demo) + a synthesis + a skeptic pass. Constraints from Arun: **new Supabase project in Mumbai**, **2+ months runway**, **Arun builds with Claude; [redacted] does docs/diagrams/testing**, **AI budget < $10**. Facts found in this session: - Repo dir only has `PROJECT_MASTER.md` + `atlas-credentials.env` (no `.gitignore`, not a git repo). The `dbms_test/*.sql`, Synopsis DOCX etc. listed in §10 are **not in the folder**. - The Test's Supabase project ("Arun-Sanjay's Project", Tokyo) is **paused**. Only **Teron** is active, and the Supabase MCP can reach Teron and all 17 projects. That's a risk. - Local: node 24, uv, docker, gh, git. **Missing:** supabase CLI, mongosh, atlas CLI, vercel CLI; python3 is 3.9 (use `uv python install 3.12`). --- ## 1. The idea: what to change **Sharpened thesis.** "Every mark has a receipt." Today a faculty member signs the paper lab sheet ("Signature of Lab Faculty") on trust. The platform makes **the rubric the schema**: - every component cell links to student **claims**; - each claim is backed by **evidence rows** (commits, document/note versions, files); - **teammates countersign** each claim; - the student **defends it in a viva generated from their own claimed work**. Everything else hangs off trustworthy contribution rows: the semester hub, skill graph, permission-aware RAG and portfolio. - Pitch: *"We don't detect AI. We make every mark traceable and every claim defensible."* - Meta hook: the evaluators grade this very project on that sheet, and the platform normalizes the sheet to BCNF and rebuilds it as live tables. - Keep the official long title on RVCE documents. Use a short product name only, e.g. **Countersign** / Attest / Provenance (check for name collisions). **Problems with the idea itself (ranked):** 1. **No single thesis.** 8 equal pillars plus 10 extras reads as "a dashboard with AI". Re-tier the features (none are deleted): - **Core:** rubric view, claims + evidence + countersign, viva practice, RLS privacy. - **Supporting:** evidence-derived skills, teammate finder, RAG, semester hub, portfolio. - **Stretch (Phase 5):** live co-editing, cross-course LLM synthesis, genealogy, work signature, LOR, recruiter, catch-up brief. 2. **"Contribution computed from commits" is gameable and spoofable.** Git author email is self-asserted, line counts reward commit spam, and pair programming, whiteboard ER work and hardware (ADLD) leave no commits. - The **claim** becomes the unit of contribution; commits and versions are *evidence*. - Identity is bound through GitHub OAuth (Supabase Auth GitHub provider → `auth.identities`), not the commit email. - No leaderboards for faculty. 3. **The problem statement implies AI-work detection.** That is unreliable and biased against non-native writers, and you build with Claude Code yourselves. - Make detection an explicit SRS non-goal. - Replace it with a declared `ai_assistance` per claim, neutral version history, and a **student-facing viva practice**. - Faculty must NOT see "AI-assisted plus low viva score", or students stop declaring. 4. **"All real work happens in the platform" is false.** Reports live in Docs/Word, diagrams in draw.io, chat in WhatsApp. - The mandatory touchpoint becomes the **milestone submission + per-component claims**. - GitHub, Obsidian and the editor become optional evidence sources, plus URL/file evidence (a Docs revision link, a draw.io export). 5. **"Evidence-derived skills" is self-declared in the actual schema.** `student_skill.level` is hand-seeded. - Add `skill_evidence` and a materialized *verified* level next to the *declared* level ("Declared 4 · Verified 2"). 6. **No named competitors.** Add a comparison table to the SRS and Midterm covering GitHub Classroom, GitHub Insights, Google Classroom/Moodle, CATME, WebPA and this project. 7. **The privacy model contradicts itself and slides into surveillance.** - "Faculty see metadata only" breaks grading of submitted work. Use 3 tiers: `private | team | submitted`. - Rename "ghost member" in the product to **"no recorded evidence yet"**. It opens the claim flow; it is never a verdict. - Add a "what my faculty sees" preview page. - DPDP Act 2023: add a consent ledger for non-grading uses, and make erasure a procedure, not a cascade. 8. **Weak pillars:** - The DIVISION teammate finder returns *clones* of you. Use **StudentSkill ÷ (Required(P) − MySkills)** to find *complements*. - Cross-course synthesis has no data behind it. Add a `course_skill` table and do it as a pure-SQL INTERSECT first, with LLM suggestions later. - Questions SQL already answers go to whitelisted SQL templates that show their SQL, not to the LLM. ## 2. Problems in design, schema and architecture (ranked) 1. **No assessment model.** Nothing stores components, submissions or marks, so the normalization of the marks sheet (C6) ends in tables that don't exist. - Add `submission`, `submission_artifact` and `assessment` at **component grain** (`usn, project, milestone_no, marks, assessed_by`), as the paper sheet does. - Criterion scores become an optional child table. - View `lab_cie_marks` computes 120→30 + 10 + 10 = 50; it is derived, never stored, and needs the rounding rule confirmed. 2. **Security isn't real yet:** - RLS is off. - Views run as owner (definer), so they bypass RLS. - A service-role backend bypasses RLS, which breaks "the AI only sees what you may see". - Realtime `postgres_changes` would leak content. - There is no `auth.users` → usn mapping. - The secrets file has no `.gitignore`. Fixes: - RLS default-deny on every table. - An `app_user` mapping table, plus helper functions (`current_usn()`, `is_team_member()`, `teaches_project()`). - `security_invoker` views and a `private` schema for notes. - RAG runs as the requesting user. - Realtime via `realtime.broadcast_changes()` with metadata-only payloads, plus RLS on `realtime.messages`. 3. **Integrity holes an examiner can INSERT live:** - a student can join 2 teams of the same project; - a T03 artifact can be filed under a P01 milestone; - a contributor or chunk author need not be a team member; - the capacity trigger only fires on INSERT (UPDATE bypasses it). Fixes: - Triggers for one-team-per-project and membership-required. - Capacity check on `INSERT OR UPDATE`. - `UNIQUE(team_id, project_id)` plus a composite FK on artifact, documented in C6 as a *deliberate, justified* denormalization. - A **constraint-violation gallery**: one failing INSERT per rule. - Do NOT add `team_member.project_id`; it would be a second 3NF violation. 4. **The capacity trigger likely over-admits under REPEATABLE READ.** The snapshot is taken before the lock wait, and the team row is locked but never updated, so no 40001 is raised. The Q37 pattern has the same flaw. - Verify on day 1. If it reproduces, it is the **headline finding of the Innovative Experiment**. - Fix the terminology in the docs: "lost update" should be *write skew / phantom*; "shared locks for dashboard reads" is wrong under MVCC. 5. **Contribution model is test-grade, not ingest-grade.** It has `DATE` columns, hand-typed IDs, no idempotency key (so GitHub redeliveries duplicate rows), no version entity, and Mongo M3 overwrites notes in place. - Use `timestamptz` and identity IDs. - Add `source`, `source_ref` and `UNIQUE(...)` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. - Add a weak entity `artifact_version`, and an immutable Mongo `note_versions` collection. 6. **No term, offering or enrollment.** `student.semester` goes stale, `course.faculty_id` means one teacher forever, and FR3 can't be computed for students without a team. - Add `academic_term`, `course_offering` and `enrollment`. - This also gives the textbook 3NF-not-BCNF example for C6. 7. **Delete semantics destroy the "permanent record".** Deleting a course cascades to contributions. - Write an FK-action matrix: CASCADE only for existence-dependent rows, RESTRICT for history, plus soft delete. 8. **No consistency contract between Mongo and Postgres** (a dual write). - Use **inbox → log → projection**: 1. The webhook calls one Postgres RPC `ingest_receive()` that inserts into `ingest_event` and `pgmq.send` in one transaction. 2. A worker upserts the raw event into Mongo (`_id = delivery_id`). 3. The worker projects it into Postgres with `ON CONFLICT`. - A consistency page diffs counts between the two databases. - Also fix the §9.3 explanation of M5: `$unwind` drops N05 because Rahul has no portfolio. 9. **The risky integrations come first in §11.3 but earn the fewest marks** (GitHub App, Hocuspocus, Obsidian, RAG). Reorder the build so the database-driven product is demoable first. - Each integration gets a replay/fixture fallback. - Hocuspocus moves to stretch; the default editor uses versioned saves with optimistic locking. - **Drop the GitHub App.** Use a plain repo webhook plus GitHub OAuth for identity. 10. **Infrastructure:** - Supabase free plan: 500 MB limit, projects pause when idle, the session pooler caps clients (~15). - Atlas M0: no MapReduce (it is deprecated), and change streams are limited. - Free hosts sleep. Fixes: - Run the big experiment matrix and the EXPLAIN bench on **local Docker PG17**; keep the cloud bench to about 300k rows. - Show MapReduce as an aggregation pipeline. - Keep-alive cron. **Grade guardrail.** `02_seed.sql` is frozen as `fixture_v1`, and CI re-runs Q1–Q37 and M1–M25 against Appendix H outputs. New real data goes in `02b_demo_seed.sql`, never inside fixture P01: - a new project **P06 "CD252IA Lab 2026-27"** with 11 milestones, where milestone_no = component number; - team T00 (Arun + [redacted]); - [redacted] added as a student; - synthetic `@example.edu` auth emails. ## 3. # Innovative Experiment — day-1 finding (2026-11-04, local PostgreSQL 17.11 in Docker)

Script: `experiments/race/rr_trigger_check.sh`. Fixture: Appendix A + B + trigger from Q35.
Two sessions race for Team Beta (T02, 3/4) last seat. Session A inserts and holds; session B's
insert blocks on the trigger's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; A commits; B resumes.

| Isolation level | Trigger only (Q35) | Q37 pattern (explicit FOR UPDATE, then INSERT) |
|---|---|---|
| READ COMMITTED  | 4/4 — B refused "Team T02 is full" | 4/4 — B refused |
| REPEATABLE READ | **5/4 — B over-admitted, no error** | **5/4 — B over-admitted, no error** |
| SERIALIZABLE    | 4/4 — B aborted, SQLSTATE 40001 (SSI pivot) | (not run) |

Why: under REPEATABLE READ the transaction snapshot is fixed at the first statement, i.e. *before*
B waits for the row lock. A only locked the team row (never updated it), so when B gets the lock
there is no update conflict (no 40001), and the COUNT(*) still reads B's old snapshot (3 members).
Under READ COMMITTED each statement in the plpgsql function takes a fresh snapshot after the lock.

Takeaway (headline of Component 10): "a correct-looking lock-then-check trigger is only correct at
READ COMMITTED." Fixes to compare: conditional `UPDATE team SET member_count = member_count+1
WHERE member_count < max_size` (writes the row → 40001 under RR), SERIALIZABLE + retry, and a
declarative `team_seat(team_id, seat_no)` UNIQUE table.
Terminology: this is write skew / a predicate phantom, not a "lost update".

# Plan — DBMS EL Platform (CD252IA): sharpened idea, upgrades, build plan, access checklist ## Context `PROJECT_MASTER.md` is the source of truth (vision, 13-table schema, seed, 37 SQL + 25 Mongo verified queries, rubric, open items). Synopsis + Component 4 (Test) are done; **no application code exists**. Arun asked for: a full plan using the whole master file, an improved idea, the biggest problems (idea + design), the best upgrades, and an exact list of what to hand over (esp. MongoDB) so Claude can run the project end-to-end. This plan merges 6 independent critiques (idea, grading, schema, architecture, privacy, demo) + a synthesis + a skeptic pass. Constraints from Arun: **new Supabase project in Mumbai**, **2+ months runway**, **Arun builds with Claude; [redacted] does docs/diagrams/testing**, **AI budget < $10**. Facts found in this session: - Repo dir only has `PROJECT_MASTER.md` + `atlas-credentials.env` (no `.gitignore`, not a git repo). The `dbms_test/*.sql`, Synopsis DOCX etc. listed in §10 are **not in the folder**. - The Test's Supabase project ("Arun-Sanjay's Project", Tokyo) is **paused**. Only **Teron** is active, and the Supabase MCP can reach Teron and all 17 projects. That's a risk. - Local: node 24, uv, docker, gh, git. **Missing:** supabase CLI, mongosh, atlas CLI, vercel CLI; python3 is 3.9 (use `uv python install 3.12`). --- ## 1. The idea: what to change **Sharpened thesis.** "Every mark has a receipt." Today a faculty member signs the paper lab sheet ("Signature of Lab Faculty") on trust. The platform makes **the rubric the schema**: - every component cell links to student **claims**; - each claim is backed by **evidence rows** (commits, document/note versions, files); - **teammates countersign** each claim; - the student **defends it in a viva generated from their own claimed work**. Everything else hangs off trustworthy contribution rows: the semester hub, skill graph, permission-aware RAG and portfolio. - Pitch: *"We don't detect AI. We make every mark traceable and every claim defensible."* - Meta hook: the evaluators grade this very project on that sheet, and the platform normalizes the sheet to BCNF and rebuilds it as live tables. - Keep the official long title on RVCE documents. Use a short product name only, e.g. **Countersign** / Attest / Provenance (check for name collisions). **Problems with the idea itself (ranked):** 1. **No single thesis.** 8 equal pillars plus 10 extras reads as "a dashboard with AI". Re-tier the features (none are deleted): - **Core:** rubric view, claims + evidence + countersign, viva practice, RLS privacy. - **Supporting:** evidence-derived skills, teammate finder, RAG, semester hub, portfolio. - **Stretch (Phase 5):** live co-editing, cross-course LLM synthesis, genealogy, work signature, LOR, recruiter, catch-up brief. 2. **"Contribution computed from commits" is gameable and spoofable.** Git author email is self-asserted, line counts reward commit spam, and pair programming, whiteboard ER work and hardware (ADLD) leave no commits. - The **claim** becomes the unit of contribution; commits and versions are *evidence*. - Identity is bound through GitHub OAuth (Supabase Auth GitHub provider → `auth.identities`), not the commit email. - No leaderboards for faculty. 3. **The problem statement implies AI-work detection.** That is unreliable and biased against non-native writers, and you build with Claude Code yourselves. - Make detection an explicit SRS non-goal. - Replace it with a declared `ai_assistance` per claim, neutral version history, and a **student-facing viva practice**. - Faculty must NOT see "AI-assisted plus low viva score", or students stop declaring. 4. **"All real work happens in the platform" is false.** Reports live in Docs/Word, diagrams in draw.io, chat in WhatsApp. - The mandatory touchpoint becomes the **milestone submission + per-component claims**. - GitHub, Obsidian and the editor become optional evidence sources, plus URL/file evidence (a Docs revision link, a draw.io export). 5. **"Evidence-derived skills" is self-declared in the actual schema.** `student_skill.level` is hand-seeded. - Add `skill_evidence` and a materialized *verified* level next to the *declared* level ("Declared 4 · Verified 2"). 6. **No named competitors.** Add a comparison table to the SRS and Midterm covering GitHub Classroom, GitHub Insights, Google Classroom/Moodle, CATME, WebPA and this project. 7. **The privacy model contradicts itself and slides into surveillance.** - "Faculty see metadata only" breaks grading of submitted work. Use 3 tiers: `private | team | submitted`. - Rename "ghost member" in the product to **"no recorded evidence yet"**. It opens the claim flow; it is never a verdict. - Add a "what my faculty sees" preview page. - DPDP Act 2023: add a consent ledger for non-grading uses, and make erasure a procedure, not a cascade. 8. **Weak pillars:** - The DIVISION teammate finder returns *clones* of you. Use **StudentSkill ÷ (Required(P) − MySkills)** to find *complements*. - Cross-course synthesis has no data behind it. Add a `course_skill` table and do it as a pure-SQL INTERSECT first, with LLM suggestions later. - Questions SQL already answers go to whitelisted SQL templates that show their SQL, not to the LLM. ## 2. Problems in design, schema and architecture (ranked) 1. **No assessment model.** Nothing stores components, submissions or marks, so the normalization of the marks sheet (C6) ends in tables that don't exist. - Add `submission`, `submission_artifact` and `assessment` at **component grain** (`usn, project, milestone_no, marks, assessed_by`), as the paper sheet does. - Criterion scores become an optional child table. - View `lab_cie_marks` computes 120→30 + 10 + 10 = 50; it is derived, never stored, and needs the rounding rule confirmed. 2. **Security isn't real yet:** - RLS is off. - Views run as owner (definer), so they bypass RLS. - A service-role backend bypasses RLS, which breaks "the AI only sees what you may see". - Realtime `postgres_changes` would leak content. - There is no `auth.users` → usn mapping. - The secrets file has no `.gitignore`. Fixes: - RLS default-deny on every table. - An `app_user` mapping table, plus helper functions (`current_usn()`, `is_team_member()`, `teaches_project()`). - `security_invoker` views and a `private` schema for notes. - RAG runs as the requesting user. - Realtime via `realtime.broadcast_changes()` with metadata-only payloads, plus RLS on `realtime.messages`. 3. **Integrity holes an examiner can INSERT live:** - a student can join 2 teams of the same project; - a T03 artifact can be filed under a P01 milestone; - a contributor or chunk author need not be a team member; - the capacity trigger only fires on INSERT (UPDATE bypasses it). Fixes: - Triggers for one-team-per-project and membership-required. - Capacity check on `INSERT OR UPDATE`. - `UNIQUE(team_id, project_id)` plus a composite FK on artifact, documented in C6 as a *deliberate, justified* denormalization. - A **constraint-violation gallery**: one failing INSERT per rule. - Do NOT add `team_member.project_id`; it would be a second 3NF violation. 4. **The capacity trigger likely over-admits under REPEATABLE READ.** The snapshot is taken before the lock wait, and the team row is locked but never updated, so no 40001 is raised. The Q37 pattern has the same flaw. - Verify on day 1. If it reproduces, it is the **headline finding of the Innovative Experiment**. - Fix the terminology in the docs: "lost update" should be *write skew / phantom*; "shared locks for dashboard reads" is wrong under MVCC. 5. **Contribution model is test-grade, not ingest-grade.** It has `DATE` columns, hand-typed IDs, no idempotency key (so GitHub redeliveries duplicate rows), no version entity, and Mongo M3 overwrites notes in place. - Use `timestamptz` and identity IDs. - Add `source`, `source_ref` and `UNIQUE(...)` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. - Add a weak entity `artifact_version`, and an immutable Mongo `note_versions` collection. 6. **No term, offering or enrollment.** `student.semester` goes stale, `course.faculty_id` means one teacher forever, and FR3 can't be computed for students without a team. - Add `academic_term`, `course_offering` and `enrollment`. - This also gives the textbook 3NF-not-BCNF example for C6. 7. **Delete semantics destroy the "permanent record".** Deleting a course cascades to contributions. - Write an FK-action matrix: CASCADE only for existence-dependent rows, RESTRICT for history, plus soft delete. 8. **No consistency contract between Mongo and Postgres** (a dual write). - Use **inbox → log → projection**: 1. The webhook calls one Postgres RPC `ingest_receive()` that inserts into `ingest_event` and `pgmq.send` in one transaction. 2. A worker upserts the raw event into Mongo (`_id = delivery_id`). 3. The worker projects it into Postgres with `ON CONFLICT`. - A consistency page diffs counts between the two databases. - Also fix the §9.3 explanation of M5: `$unwind` drops N05 because Rahul has no portfolio. 9. **The risky integrations come first in §11.3 but earn the fewest marks** (GitHub App, Hocuspocus, Obsidian, RAG). Reorder the build so the database-driven product is demoable first. - Each integration gets a replay/fixture fallback. - Hocuspocus moves to stretch; the default editor uses versioned saves with optimistic locking. - **Drop the GitHub App.** Use a plain repo webhook plus GitHub OAuth for identity. 10. **Infrastructure:** - Supabase free plan: 500 MB limit, projects pause when idle, the session pooler caps clients (~15). - Atlas M0: no MapReduce (it is deprecated), and change streams are limited. - Free hosts sleep. Fixes: - Run the big experiment matrix and the EXPLAIN bench on **local Docker PG17**; keep the cloud bench to about 300k rows. - Show MapReduce as an aggregation pipeline. - Keep-alive cron. **Grade guardrail.** `02_seed.sql` is frozen as `fixture_v1`, and CI re-runs Q1–Q37 and M1–M25 against Appendix H outputs. # Innovative Experiment — day-1 finding (2026-11-04, local PostgreSQL 17.11 in Docker)

Script: `experiments/race/rr_trigger_check.sh`. Fixture: Appendix A + B + trigger from Q35.
Two sessions race for Team Beta (T02, 3/4) last seat. Session A inserts and holds; session B's
insert blocks on the trigger's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; A commits; B resumes.

| Isolation level | Trigger only (Q35) | Q37 pattern (explicit FOR UPDATE, then INSERT) |
|---|---|---|
| READ COMMITTED  | 4/4 — B refused "Team T02 is full" | 4/4 — B refused |
| REPEATABLE READ | **5/4 — B over-admitted, no error** | **5/4 — B over-admitted, no error** |
| SERIALIZABLE    | 4/4 — B aborted, SQLSTATE 40001 (SSI pivot) | (not run) |

Why: under REPEATABLE READ the transaction snapshot is fixed at the first statement, i.e. *before*
B waits for the row lock. A only locked the team row (never updated it), so when B gets the lock
there is no update conflict (no 40001), and the COUNT(*) still reads B's old snapshot (3 members).
Under READ COMMITTED each statement in the plpgsql function takes a fresh snapshot after the lock.

Takeaway (headline of Component 10): "a correct-looking lock-then-check trigger is only correct at
READ COMMITTED." Fixes to compare: conditional `UPDATE team SET member_count = member_count+1
WHERE member_count < max_size` (writes the row → 40001 under RR), SERIALIZABLE + retry, and a
declarative `team_seat(team_id, seat_no)` UNIQUE table.
Terminology: this is write skew / a predicate phantom, not a "lost update".
